chain_proof: DROPPED #1 (the CEB) — the lighting.created emit names six keys total, four of which are envelope (commandId, commandType, levelId, id). Only `kind` and `origin` are element data.

DROPPED #2 (the command itself) — packages/command-registry/src/lighting/CreateLightingCommand.ts writes only fixtureType, position, rotation, hostId, tags, properties (:124-132). Thirteen of the L0 fields have no slot in the command payload at all, so the loss predates the bridge.

SUBSTITUTED — LightingFragmentBuilder does not read the authored photometry. It looks the fixture up in a CATALOGUE: :1986 `const intensity = data.emission?.intensity ?? sceneIntensityFor(photo, this._isNight);` and :1989 `const colorHex = kelvinToHex(photo.kelvin);` where `photo` comes from `photometryForFixture` (FixturePhotometry.ts). Line 334 states it outright: 'Lens tint, DERIVED from the row's kelvin — never authored.'
fidelity.honesty_verdict: SPLIT. The SUBSTITUTION is honest — the builder says in its own comments that colour and brightness come from the catalogue row and are 'never authored', and that is a defensible LOD-200 design (LightingTypes.ts:250-261 defends ONE `lod200Overrides` block over twenty param interfaces, precisely to avoid twenty chances to drop a field on load). The DROP is not — the L0 schema authors kelvin, lumens, beamAngleDeg, intensity, colour, dropLength and isEmergency as if they were settable, no gate refuses them, and nothing warns that they will be ignored.
fidelity.user_visible_consequence: A pendant authored at 2700 K with a 3 m drop and 1200 lm renders at the catalogue's kelvin, the catalogue's lumens and no drop. An emergency luminaire (`isEmergency`) is indistinguishable from a normal one.
